_note: The DSX Scene PARSE corpus (dsx-scene.md P1): markup → the typed scene IR. THE LAW: the <scene> subtree is owned by the scene element — its children parse into typed nodes (camera · light · group · box · sphere · plane · model · text3d · anchor), attribute VALUES keep their JSE holes verbatim (the IR is store-agnostic; a resolver interpolates at use time), and every default is pinned HERE so three renderers cannot drift: scene mode '3d', background '#000000'; camera position '0 0 5', look-at '0 0 0', fov 60, near 0.1, far 1000, size 5 (the 2d half-extent); light kind 'ambient', intensity 1, color '#ffffff', position '0 0 0' (a directional light's position is its direction toward the origin); geometry position '0 0 0', rotation '0 0 0', scale '1 1 1'; box size '1 1 1'; sphere radius 1; plane size '1 1' (width height, facing +Z); color '#ffffff'. FAILURE IS A VALUE (Article 7): a malformed scalar/triple falls back to its default with one diagnostic; an unknown tag inside <scene> is SKIPPED with one diagnostic (never a crash, never a phantom node); an unknown light kind falls back to 'ambient' with one diagnostic. Case shape: `markup` = the .dsx snippet (parsed by each runner's own XML parser — StackXML twins); `vars` = the hole resolver map (default empty); `expect` = the resolved IR subset asserted structurally — `mode`/`background` for the root, `nodes` = recursive {kind, id?, and any resolved typed props: position/rotation/scale (triples), size (box triple / plane pair), radius/fov/near/far/intensity (scalars), kind, color, raw (the UNresolved authored string when a case pins hole retention)}; `diagnostics` = expected count (absent = 0). Runners: TS (per-PR); Kotlin/Swift are the P2 row of dsx-scene.md.
